summary.oneLiner: Best-ever quarter on highest-ever vessel deployment (record revenue/PAT) with day-rates at all-time highs and net cash; growth story is fleet-driven (Swordfish full-year FY27 + Agastya + Anant) and ONGC/IMR-mix-led, but earnings are lumpy quarter-to-quarter (dry-docks, contract changeovers) — management explicitly says judge on a YEARLY basis.

thesis (one line): Best-ever quarter on highest-ever vessel deployment (record revenue/PAT) with day-rates at all-time highs and net cash; growth story is fleet-driven (Swordfish full-year FY27 + Agastya + Anant) and ONGC/IMR-mix-led, but earnings are lumpy quarter-to-quarter (dry-docks, contract changeovers) — management explicitly says judge on a YEARLY basis.
scorecard (q3 fy26, consolidated unless:
| Metric | Q3 FY26 | Q3 FY25 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue (consol) | ₹331 cr | ₹139 cr | **+138%** | Best-ever quarterly revenue |
| Revenue (standalone) | ₹317 cr | ₹133 cr | +139% | |
| EBITDA (consol) | ₹150 cr | ₹34 cr | +341% | ~45% margin |
| EBITDA (standalone) | ₹144 cr | ₹36 cr | +300% | ~45% margin |
| PAT (consol) | ₹100 cr | –₹3 cr (loss) | turnaround | Reported = normalized (no separate norm given) |
| PAT (standalone) | ₹101 cr | ₹2 cr | huge | |
| **9M Rev (consol)** | ₹670 cr | ₹473 cr | +42% | |
| **9M Rev (standalone)** | ₹631 cr | ₹452 cr | +40% | |
| **9M EBITDA (consol)** | ₹285 cr | ₹143 cr | +99% | |
| **9M PAT (consol)** | ₹150 cr | ₹47 cr | +219% | |
| **9M PAT (standalone)** | ₹155 cr | ₹57 cr | +172% | |
| ROCE / ROE (consol) | 15% / 16% | — | — | 9M / annualized basis |
| **Net cash** | Net debt ≈ **zero or negative (net cash)** | — | — | Despite ₹850 cr Agastya debt + planned Anant term loan |

**Day-rates / utilization (CONCRETE):**
- **Swordfish day-rate: ~$75,000/day** (most capable vessel — bigger crane/accommodation than Anant).
- **Anant day-rate: ~$45,000/day** (newer but smaller-spec vessel).
- **Agastya:** 5-year tenure contract, high utilization certainty; commenced ops with ONGC via HAL Offshore post dry-docking.
- **Highest-ever vessel deployment** in company history this quarter — key driver of record results.
- Charter rates at "highest levels seen so far"; management expects them to **sustain / stay steady** near term (mix of long-term + short-term contracts).

**One-offs / exceptional items:**
- **+₹22 cr+ exceptional benefit** in Q3 from the **Goodman** vessel (HAL Offshore-owned; contract booked in Seamec, vessel rented from HAL at marginal cost) — explicitly flagged as exceptional, not recurring.
- Overseas (Dubai sub, 1 vessel): revenue ₹15 cr; **net PAT impact ≈ –₹2 cr (drag)** due to subsidiary expenses.
- Forex: not separately quantified.
- **Q4 FY26 headwind flagged:** Seamec Paladin in dry-dock ~2 months (~70 days, Dubai, statutory) + Seamec Diamond (smaller supply vessel) also dry-docking → lower Q4 revenue/profit.
guidance (critical):
- **Day-rate outlook:** Rates at highs; management expects them to remain **steady/sustained** "for some more time" — no normalization signalled near-term.
- **Utilization outlook:** Record deployment; aiming for more **IMR (inspection-maintenance-repair) contracts** which give full-year (incl. monsoon) deployment vs EPC (no monsoon work) to "streamline the quarters."
- **Fleet additions:** **Swordfish full-year contribution in FY27** (only part-year in FY26); **Agastya** now deployed; **Anant acquisition to close within FY26 (Q4), deployed Q1 FY27** with revenue from then.
- **Order/contract inflow:** Strategy to migrate new HAL Offshore contracts into Seamec (grow Seamec's share; HAL book to deplete as contracts expire).
- **FY27 = a "year of GROWTH"** (Swordfish full year + Agastya + Anant), per management — explicitly NOT a consolidation year.
- Management repeatedly: **judge performance YEAR-over-YEAR, not quarter-over-quarter** (dry-docks/changeovers cause lumpiness).
order book & pipeline (charters / epc):
- No consolidated order-book ₹ figure disclosed (vessel-charter contract model). Contract visibility:
  - **Agastya: 5-year charter** with ONGC (via HAL Offshore) — long visibility.
  - Mix of **long-term + short-term** charters across the fleet → "steady revenue visibility."
  - Seamec III sailed 25-Dec-2025 for **Phase-2 Pipeline Replacement Project + DSF II** projects.
  - Completed turnkey revamping of **ONGC's NLM9 platform** ahead of schedule (Q3).
- **₹1,000 cr MoU with DG Shipping** (vessel acquisition commitment over next 2–3 years; one or more vessels; funding case-by-case — internal accrual or mix).
- **OALP-VIII:** ONGC won 7 of 10 blocks → exploration-positive, but **commercialization 4–6 years out**; no immediate tender upside for Seamec.
segment (vessel charter / imr vs epc):
- **IMR contracts = higher-margin, full-year deployment (incl. monsoon), no off-hire** — strategic preference; all new high-value assets assumed/deployed on IMR (only profitable that way).
- **EPC = 2 older-vintage vessels** (zero book value); don't work in monsoon; lower revenue but any business improves ROC/ROE/bottom line since assets are at ₹0.
- Target IMR/EPC mix over 3–5 yrs: directionally toward IMR; no hard ratio given.
growth / optionality:
- **Fleet expansion:** Swordfish (full year FY27), Agastya (live), Anant (Q1 FY27), + ₹1,000 cr DG Shipping MoU for 1+ more vessels over 2–3 yrs.
- **ONGC / offshore capex tailwind:** India $100bn upstream push; refining 260→300 MMTPA; ONGC-RIL offshore-resource-sharing MoU; OALP-VIII (long-dated).
- **Inorganic + organic:** open to acquisitions; near-term growth from existing assets + Anant.
- **HAL Offshore migration:** future contracts to be bid into Seamec → captive pipeline transferring from parent.
- **Exports/overseas:** Dubai sub operating (currently a small drag); conscious effort to consolidate core and trim overseas losses.
margins & cost:
- ~45% EBITDA margin (₹150 cr on ₹331 cr consol) — IMR-mix + record utilization + Goodman one-off.
- Risk/breakdown contingency **priced into day-rates** (not insured — high-value charter premiums prohibitive); a margin buffer kept for breakdowns.
- IMR > EPC on margin; zero-book EPC vessels are pure margin accretion when working.
capex (new vessels):
- **Agastya: acquired for ~$23 million**, funded internal sources + **₹850 cr debt** repayable over **8 years** (quarterly installments).
- **Anant:** funded **50:50 own funds : term loan**; term loan tenure 5–8 yrs (decided at disbursement).
- Both loans expected to be **prepaid within 3–4 years** from higher accruals.
capital allocation:
- **Net debt ≈ zero / net cash** despite Agastya ₹850 cr loan; debt-equity & debt-EBITDA "very healthy" — comfortable carrying some debt.
- Surplus cash priority: **(1) acquire growth assets (Anant via internal accruals to large extent), (2) debt reduction** with leftover.
- No dividend discussion on call.
risks:
- **Earnings lumpiness:** dry-docks (Paladin + Diamond in Q4; 3 more — Seamec III/Princess/Glorious — in FY27, but in monsoon to limit disruption), contract changeovers, vessel off-hire.
- **Vessel/machinery breakdown risk** (24/7 ops; last-quarter breakdown addressed, no client penalty, but recurring breakdowns would be the real concern; not insured).
- **Offshore-capex / oil-price cyclicality**; ONGC dependence (single dominant customer ecosystem).
- **Related-party / HAL Offshore concentration** (needs ONGC + shareholder approvals — Anant delayed ~1 year over RPT-limit/ONGC approvals).
- **Aging fleet:** DG Shipping age-norms currently exempt DSVs, but prudent recycle-vs-operate decisions ahead.
- One-off dependence (Goodman ₹22 cr+) inflates the optical Q3 base.
mgmt tone: - Confident/upbeat — "landmark quarter," "best ever," "strongest quarter to date," "FY27 a year of growth." Disciplined messaging: repeatedly steers investors to YEARLY view; transparent about Goodman one-off and Q4 dry-dock drag.
non-obvious:
- The **Goodman vessel (₹22 cr+)** is structurally interesting: management is deliberately **migrating HAL Offshore's contracts/vessels into Seamec** (renting vessels from parent at marginal cost), so the listed entity captures economics that historically sat in the parent — a recurring value-transfer lever, even if this specific contract was a one-off.
- **No insurance on high-value charters** — breakdown risk is self-priced into day-rates; a structural margin/risk feature, not a gap.
- Anant's lower **$45k** rate vs Swordfish **$75k** is spec/scope/risk-driven (newer ≠ pricier) — refutes naive "new vessel = premium rate."
- OALP-VIII / new ONGC blocks are a **4–6 year** optionality, not a near-term catalyst.
challenges → beneficiaries:
- ✅ India upstream/offshore capex push, ONGC OALP-VIII & ONGC-RIL offshore resource-sharing → long-dated demand for DSV/IMR vessels (Seamec, HAL-linked operators).
- ⭐ DG Shipping age-norm exemption for DSVs → incumbents with older DSV fleets (Seamec) retain operating runway.
- (Beneficiary list otherwise empty — single-name offshore charter play.)

themes.title: Naval shipbuilding & maritime
themes.need: A multi-decade naval order book and indigenous warship/submarine build, plus the naval-equipment supply chain (HVAC/chillers, mechanical seals, marine gearing) and maritime services, underpin the theme. GRSE carries a large RFP pipeline (~INR1.5 lakh cr referenced); SHREE REFRIGERATIONS 544458 supplies naval HVAC; SEALMATIC 543782 naval/submarine seals; ELECON defence-marine gearing; KMEW/SEAMECLTD/DREDGECORP maritime services.
themes.driver: Fresh MoD warship/submarine orders + naval-equipment indigenization inflow; maritime-infra/offshore contract wins.

themes.title: Oil & Gas - gas economy (CGD/LNG) + refining/upstream
themes.need: India's gas-economy push now collides with an outright policy reversal. ATGL grew volume 13% to 303 MMSCM and revenue 27% to INR 1,908cr, yet EBITDA FELL sequentially to INR 281cr (~14.7% margin, from INR 310cr) because the government withdrew the pooled-gas mechanism after the West Asia 'peace deal', pushing ATGL to ~15% spot volumes with Brent above $107/bbl; management also noted NWG price is 12% of the Indian crude basket, so a 62% domestic mix protects far less than it looks, and CNG station adds slowed to +5 from +25 in Q4 even as CNG demand grows ~30%. The same shock ran the other way for integrated refining: RELIANCE delivered O2C EBITDA of INR 17,000cr (+17%) THROUGH the Strait-of-Hormuz closure at 96-97% throughput while Asian peers ran 15-20% below capacity, with ethane+ROGC at ~70% of ethylene feed as distillate cracks blew out (gas oil $16 to $63, ATF $14 to $62). MGL/GUJGASLTD/IGL/IRMENERGY carry the same CGD margin squeeze; PETRONET/OIL/ONGC/IOC ride LNG-infra + domestic-gas; CHENNPETRO/MRPL ride GRM cracks; DEEPINDS/JINDRILL/SEAMECLTD on ONGC E&P capex; AEGISLOG/AEGISVOPAK add LPG/gas terminalling.
themes.driver: Whether the pooled/APM gas-allocation mechanism is restored (the single biggest CGD earnings variable); LNG spot price and Brent; GRM/distillate cracks; ONGC rig tenders & day-rates.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Describes itself as 'a formidable player in offshore shipping backed by India's largest fleet of multi-support vessels', a leading provider of specialised engineering services (subsea and marine operations) to the offshore oil & gas industry.
- Long operating history with ONGC and international oil majors; clientele includes ONGC, L&T, POSH, Safeen Al Behar, Zamil Offshore, Clipper Petroleum, Lamprell Energy, Mermaid, Eagle Bulk Shipping and Westfield Energy. High entry barriers from specialised equipment and certification requirements.
- Part of the MMG Group since HAL Offshore acquired the company from the erstwhile Technip India group in 2014; promoter holding ~72.72%.
- Cites strong MMG parentage as strengthening financial position and market reputation, with technical expertise and financial strength positioning it favourably in the tendering process.

management_tone.body: - Confident/upbeat — "landmark quarter," "best ever," "strongest quarter to date," "FY27 a year of growth." Disciplined messaging: repeatedly steers investors to YEARLY view; transparent about Goodman one-off and Q4 dry-dock drag.

risks.title: Risks
risks.body:
- **Earnings lumpiness:** dry-docks (Paladin + Diamond in Q4; 3 more — Seamec III/Princess/Glorious — in FY27, but in monsoon to limit disruption), contract changeovers, vessel off-hire.
- **Vessel/machinery breakdown risk** (24/7 ops; last-quarter breakdown addressed, no client penalty, but recurring breakdowns would be the real concern; not insured).
- **Offshore-capex / oil-price cyclicality**; ONGC dependence (single dominant customer ecosystem).
- **Related-party / HAL Offshore concentration** (needs ONGC + shareholder approvals — Anant delayed ~1 year over RPT-limit/ONGC approvals).
- **Aging fleet:** DG Shipping age-norms currently exempt DSVs, but prudent recycle-vs-operate decisions ahead.
- One-off dependence (Goodman ₹22 cr+) inflates the optical Q3 base.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious
non_obvious.body:
- The **Goodman vessel (₹22 cr+)** is structurally interesting: management is deliberately **migrating HAL Offshore's contracts/vessels into Seamec** (renting vessels from parent at marginal cost), so the listed entity captures economics that historically sat in the parent — a recurring value-transfer lever, even if this specific contract was a one-off.
- **No insurance on high-value charters** — breakdown risk is self-priced into day-rates; a structural margin/risk feature, not a gap.
- Anant's lower **$45k** rate vs Swordfish **$75k** is spec/scope/risk-driven (newer ≠ pricier) — refutes naive "new vessel = premium rate."
- OALP-VIII / new ONGC blocks are a **4–6 year** optionality, not a near-term catalyst.

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries
challenges.body:
- ✅ India upstream/offshore capex push, ONGC OALP-VIII & ONGC-RIL offshore resource-sharing → long-dated demand for DSV/IMR vessels (Seamec, HAL-linked operators).
- ⭐ DG Shipping age-norm exemption for DSVs → incumbents with older DSV fleets (Seamec) retain operating runway.
- (Beneficiary list otherwise empty — single-name offshore charter play.)

---

qoq_log.title: QoQ Log
qoq_log.body: - **Q3 FY26 (this call):** Record qtr — consol rev ₹331 cr (+138% YoY), EBITDA ₹150 cr, PAT ₹100 cr (vs ₹3 cr loss YoY); highest-ever deployment. Day-rates: Swordfish ~$75k, Anant ~$45k. Agastya (5-yr, $23m, ₹850 cr/8yr debt) deployed. Anant acquisition to close Q4, deploy Q1FY27 (50:50 funding). Goodman one-off +₹22 cr+. Net cash. Q4 guided softer (Paladin + Diamond dry-docks). ₹1,000 cr DG Shipping MoU for 1+ vessels over 2–3 yrs. FY27 = growth year (Swordfish full year). Manage to yearly, not quarterly.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Acquisition] Acquired Aarey Organic Industries Private Limited to carry out manufacturing, selling, importing, exporting and distributing various types of chemicals — a diversification outside the core marine/offshore business.
- [Policy Tailwind] Government approved the 'Samudra Manthan' National Offshore Exploration Scheme with a total outlay of ₹84,084 crore through FY2030-31, offering financial assistance of up to 50% of eligible exploration costs — a structural demand driver for offshore service providers like SEAMEC.
- [Industry Demand] ONGC floated offshore vessel tenders worth ₹1,000+ crore under 'Make in India'; India's offshore facilities pipeline includes 25 installations and 1,000+ km of subsea pipelines over the next three years.
